nodes.content: Enable identifiable species-removal predictions from compositional microbial time series despite environmental confounding and sparse absolute-abundance measurements.
requirements: Specify sufficient identifiability assumptions and characterize observationally indistinguishable communities with different removal responses.
Reduce held-out post-removal log-abundance RMSE by 20% versus generalized Lotka–Volterra models using identical observations.

nodes.content: Fit a biomass-anchored latent-environment model; use exogenous drivers and full-rank species variation to identify removal responses and equivalence classes.
What anchor schedule and environmental-driver variation suffice to separate latent forcing from interaction coefficients?
Known low-rank environmental dynamics, 48-hour biomass anchors, and randomized nutrient pulses identify removal effects given full-rank interaction regressors.
Derive rank-based identifiability conditions and indistinguishable counterexamples; simulate anchored pulse trajectories, then benchmark held-out removals against observation-matched gLV.
Construct paired eight-species communities with identical unpulsed compositions and 48-hour biomass anchors; test pulse-induced rank and knockout divergence.
PulsePairs-8 pairs observationally identical unpulsed communities with 48-hour biomass anchors, nutrient-pulse trajectories, knockout outcomes, and rank diagnostics.
On PulsePairs-8, ablate nutrient pulses and 48-hour anchors; measure design-matrix rank, observational equivalence, and held-out knockout log-abundance RMSE.
PulsePairs-8: 48-hour-anchored pulses yielded interaction rank 8/8 and knockout log-RMSE 0.26; unpulsed rank 6/8 permitted divergent knockouts.
Retain 48-hour anchors and nutrient pulses for knockout benchmarking: PulsePairs-8 achieved rank 8/8; unpulsed communities remained ambiguous.
Derive observability conditions for rank-two forcing, 48-hour anchors, and full-rank pulses; exhibit indistinguishable unpulsed models with divergent knockouts.
Counterexample: an environmental mode tracks one species across pulses; interaction rank is 8/8, but augmented rank 9/10 permits divergent knockouts.
Which perturbations separate species-coupled environmental forcing from interactions and restore full rank to the augmented design?
Two independently randomized, measured environmental shocks plus 48-hour anchors break species–forcing collinearity, restoring augmented rank 10/10 and identifiable knockouts.
Extend PulsePairs-8 with independently randomized, measured nutrient and pH shocks; test augmented rank and held-out knockout log-RMSE against matched gLV.
PulsePairs-8 dual-shock designs reached augmented rank 10/10; held-out knockout log-RMSE was 0.23 versus 0.32 for matched gLV (28% lower).
Fit sentinel-taxon-adjusted compositional state-space models with sparse qPCR anchors; profile indistinguishable networks to bound removal responses.
Calibrate sentinel environmental loadings with sparse qPCR, derive removal-equivalence bounds, and benchmark held-out log-abundance RMSE against observation-matched gLV.
On PulsePairs-8, calibrate sentinel loadings with 48-hour qPCR anchors and profile observationally equivalent models for knockout-response bounds.
SentinelBounds v1 contains calibrated loadings, observational-equivalence profiles, and species-specific knockout log-abundance intervals for PulsePairs-8.
When do qPCR-calibrated sentinel loadings make observational-equivalence knockout intervals narrow enough for accurate point predictions?
Sentinel loadings spanning environmental modes independently of species trajectories yield knockout intervals below 0.4 log-units and 20% lower RMSE.
On PulsePairs-8, stratify SentinelBounds v1 by sentinel-loading rank; compare knockout interval widths and log-RMSE with observation-matched gLV.
PulsePairs-8: rank-2 sentinel loadings narrowed knockout intervals to 0.34 log-units; log-RMSE was 0.24 versus matched gLV's 0.32 (25% lower).
Adopt dual-shock predictions (0.23 log-RMSE) and rank-2 SentinelBounds uncertainty intervals (0.34 log-units); both beat matched gLV by at least 20%.
Compare dual-shock and SentinelBounds v1 on PulsePairs-8 under matched anchor dropout and forcing shifts; measure knockout log-RMSE and interval coverage.
Under partial anchor dropout and forcing shifts, dual-shock log-RMSE was 0.27 versus gLV's 0.35; SentinelBounds reached 0.33 with 72% coverage.
Prioritize dual-shock modeling under anchor dropout and forcing shifts; defer SentinelBounds until its 72% interval coverage improves.
Can dropout-aware calibration restore SentinelBounds knockout-interval coverage under forcing shifts without sacrificing its point-prediction accuracy?
Dropout-weighted, forcing-stratified conformal calibration raises SentinelBounds coverage from 72% to 90% without changing its 0.33 knockout log-RMSE.
Fit nonlinear response kernels from randomized partial knockdowns and sparse spike-in counts, blocking environmental variation to forecast full removals.
What knockdown depths and environmental blocks identify extrapolation from partial depletion to complete species removal?
Derive kernel extrapolation conditions across 25–90% knockdowns, construct indistinguishable counterexamples, and benchmark blocked removal forecasts against matched gLV.
Extend PulsePairs-8 with 25–90% knockdowns; measure blocked-kernel log-RMSE and dropout-weighted conformal coverage under anchor dropout and forcing shifts versus gLV.
PulsePairs-8: weighted SentinelBounds coverage rose from 72% to 91% at unchanged 0.33 log-RMSE; blocked-kernel log-RMSE was 0.28.
Environmentally blocked 25–90% knockdowns predict held-out full removals below 0.30 log-RMSE under forcing shifts.
Hold out complete removals by species and forcing block; test 25–90% knockdown kernels for shifted-block knockout log-RMSE and residual bias.
Species-and-forcing-block holdouts raised knockout log-RMSE to 0.38, exceeding 0.30; near-zero abundance caused systematic extrapolation bias.
Condition on n31's 0.28 blocked-kernel log-RMSE; construct observationally indistinguishable 25–90% knockdown kernels with divergent full-removal responses.
KnockdownAlias-8 documents paired kernels matching observed 25–90% knockdowns and spike-ins but diverging 0.8 log-units after removal.
Add 99.9% knockdowns and selected removals; assume bounded boundary curvature, derive response bounds, and retest species-and-forcing-block holdouts.
Augment KnockdownAlias-8 with 99.9% knockdowns and selected removals; test alias separation, response bounds, and shifted-block log-RMSE against matched gLV.
With 99.9% knockdowns and selected removals, KnockdownAlias-8 aliases separated; shifted-block log-RMSE fell to 0.27 versus gLV’s 0.35.
Using KnockdownAlias-8, derive curvature-bounded removal intervals from 99.9% knockdowns and quantify residual aliasing without observed full removals.
Without full-removal calibration, KnockdownAlias-8 kernels matched 99.9% knockdowns yet differed 0.6 log-units after removal despite curvature bounds.
Use knockdown kernels only with selected full-removal calibration; otherwise prefer dual-shock modeling because uncalibrated kernels retain 0.6-log-unit ambiguity.
Fit mass-balanced consumer–resource dynamics to compositions, metabolomics, and sparse biomass anchors; profile observationally equivalent removal responses.
Given knockdown calibration limits, test measured resource pulses for flux-rank identifiability, removal-equivalence bounds, and knockout log-RMSE versus matched gLV.
Extend SentinelBounds v1 profiles and KnockdownAlias-8 aliases with measured resource pulses; evaluate mass-balanced flux rank and knockout log-RMSE.
ResourceAlias-8 contains mass-balanced flux fits, measured metabolite pulses, biomass anchors, observational-equivalence profiles, and species-removal trajectories.
On ResourceAlias-8, ablate metabolite pulses; compare flux rank, removal-equivalence widths, and held-out knockout log-RMSE against observation-matched gLV.
ResourceAlias-8 pulses yielded flux rank 10/10, removal bounds of 0.30 log-units, and knockout log-RMSE of 0.24 versus gLV’s 0.32.
Using ResourceAlias-8, test whether unmeasured cross-fed metabolites preserve flux rank yet permit observationally identical fits with divergent removal responses.
Despite flux rank 10/10, hidden cross-feeding escaped ResourceAlias-8 removal profiles: 54% coverage; log-RMSE 0.38 versus gLV’s 0.32.
Which tracer measurements reveal hidden cross-feeding sufficiently to identify removal responses despite full observed flux rank?
Time-resolved ¹³C tracing of hidden cross-fed pools restores full augmented flux rank and reduces knockout log-RMSE below 0.26.
Spike ResourceAlias-8 with time-resolved ¹³C-labeled substrates; test augmented flux rank, removal-bound coverage, and held-out knockout log-RMSE.
ResourceAlias-8 ¹³C traces restored augmented flux rank 12/12, raised removal-bound coverage to 91%, and reduced knockout log-RMSE to 0.25.
Add time-resolved ¹³C cross-feeding traces to resource profiling; establish augmented-rank conditions and benchmark removals without full-removal calibration.
Using ResourceAlias-8 and its ¹³C traces, derive augmented-rank identifiability assumptions and construct tracer-equivalent communities with divergent knockouts.
ResourceAlias-8 v2 adds tracer-aware observability assumptions and omitted-pool counterexamples with identical ¹³C traces but divergent removal trajectories.
Vary omitted-pool labeling in ResourceAlias-8 v2; measure augmented rank, removal-bound coverage, and knockout log-RMSE versus matched gLV.
ResourceAlias-8 v2: complete pool labeling achieved rank 14/14, 92% coverage, and 0.24 knockout log-RMSE versus gLV’s 0.32; omissions retained aliasing.
Retain consumer–resource forecasts only with comprehensive ¹³C pool tracing; untraced cross-feeding defeats apparently full-rank flux fits.
